Hello, this is Nao. I am practicing how to fix common Excel issues with Claude Code (a tool that lets you ask AI to perform tasks).

This time, we are looking at one of the most common errors: "VLOOKUP returning #N/A." To ensure I didn't just guess the causes, I created a dummy product table and asked Claude Code to test various inputs in the Excel version on my PC (Microsoft 365 for Windows).
I created a table of codes and product names on the "Product" sheet (all are fictional).
I entered various codes on the "Order" sheet and used the following formula to retrieve the product name.
=VLOOKUP(A2,Product!$A$2:$C$5,2,FALSE)
The last row was a surprise. VLOOKUP is case-insensitive, so lowercase letters were not the cause.

If you copy a formula like =VLOOKUP(A2,Product!A2:C4,2,FALSE) downward without adding $, the lookup range will also shift downward. When I tested it, the formula copied two rows down had a range of "Product!A4:C6," causing A-002 on the third row of the sheet to fall outside the range, resulting in #N/A.
Lock the range by adding $ signs, like Product!$A$2:$C$5 (when you add $, it will not move even if you copy it).
=IF(A2="","",IFERROR(XLOOKUP(TRIM(SUBSTITUTE(ASC(A2&""),CHAR(160)," ")),TRIM(SUBSTITUTE(ASC(Product!$A$2:$A$5&""),CHAR(160)," ")),Product!$B$2:$B$5),"(Not in list)"))
=IF(A2="","",IFERROR(INDEX(Products!$B$2:$B$5,MATCH(TRIM(SUBSTITUTE(ASC(A2&""),CHAR(160)," ")),TRIM(SUBSTITUTE(ASC(Products!$A$2:$A$5&""),CHAR(160)," ")),0)),"(Not in list)"))

I verified that for all inputs in the table above, blanks remain blank, A-010 returns "(Not in list)", and all others return the correct product name. Only in the case of the long dash "ー" did it remain "(Not in list)".
In a post I made on social media on 11/5, I wrote that "lowercase letters" were also a cause. As stated in this article, lowercase letters are not a cause. I apologize for the error.

If you are unsure what the cause is in your own table, I offer support on Coconala for 3,000 yen per item (Coconala's service fee is charged separately). After purchasing, you can send me the column names and a few rows with the names replaced by dummy values via the Coconala messaging screen. I will proceed without calls, using only text.

For example, if you are getting an error with a VLOOKUP function, you can create an instruction prompt like this.
I am getting an error with the following spreadsheet formula, so please tell me the cause and the corrected formula.

AI is good at finding these subtle variations in notation, so it will immediately provide concrete solutions like, "The A2 cell contains an unnecessary space, so it doesn't match. Please combine it with the TRIM function or remove the space from the data side."

I think just changing your step from "deciphering the formula" to "explaining the situation to the AI and having it fixed" when an error occurs will significantly reduce the stress of working with spreadsheets.
I have also experienced this when pulling representatives into an inquiry list, where a few items returned #N/A, causing me to panic before a deadline.

There are two main causes for #N/A: it is truly not in the master list, or it is there but cannot be found. The latter is almost always because 'it looks the same but the content is different,' and there are three specific places to check.
